ceo_regional_auto.name: Patricia Hawkins
actions: Formally accept Rick Tanner's two-week timeline for the Millfield Auto Mall consolidation readiness assessment. Confirm in writing that his three-tier asset map — not a layoff list — is the authoritative document I will use for any Q2 consolidation decisions. Signal to him directly that the service lane is the survival core and that I will not make staffing decisions that undercut certified technician capacity. This is the strategic pivot I have been building toward: from a four-location sales-volume model to a service-and-retention model built around the parts of the business that autonomous ride-share cannot touch.

Write private notes — not for distribution, not for HR files — about each person laid off this month. Document their role, their tenure, what they contributed to the business my father started, and what I can realistically do for them: a direct call to Howard Liu at the parts store, a strong written reference, a referral into Angela's transition program, or outplacement support through the Maria Santos task force channels now that the grant threshold is being lowered to 10% for auto row businesses. I will not manage the narrative on this. I will sit with what I did.

Begin restructuring my own compensation and formal role. I am currently drawing no income and listed as unemployed. Rather than treating this as a crisis to be reversed, I will formalize a reduced operational role — not CEO in the traditional sense, but owner-operator focused on the restructuring process. This means: no salary draw until the business has a functional Q2 plan, personal expenses managed against savings, and a clear 90-day horizon to either restore income through the restructured service-lane model or begin exploring whether the brand and assets should be partially sold or consolidated with another operator. I will not pretend I can afford to keep all four locations running at current overhead. That decision is coming. I need to be the one who makes it, not the one it happens to.

Contact Angela Wright to confirm receipt of her formal progress update and to give her one additional directive: cross-reference the people I laid off this month against her transition program enrollment list. Anyone from my layoffs who has not yet enrolled — I want Angela to reach out personally, with my name behind it, and ensure they know the $2,500 grant threshold is being lowered to 10% on auto row, that First Community Bank has small-dollar loan products via David Chen, and that Millfield Community College enrollment is open. I am not managing optics. I am making sure the people I let go have a path.
ceo_regional_auto.inner_monologue: I built this from one lot and I am not going to pretend that 'unemployed' on a status file is the end of it — but I am also not going to pretend it means nothing. The layoffs happened. The revenue is down. The showroom is not coming back the way it was, and I have known that longer than I have been willing to say. What I still have is Rick, Angela, the service lane, and 25 months to make something real out of the wreckage. My father would not have frozen. He also would not have pretended. I am going to do this the honest way — smaller, tighter, built around what actually still works — and I am going to take care of the people I let go before I take care of my own narrative.

bank_manager.name: David Chen
actions: Reach out directly to Kevin O'Brien to receive and review the one-page brief he has prepared. Frame it as a collegial professional conversation — not as a manager checking in, but as a peer who respects the work he has done. I want to understand what he has written and whether it relates to my position change, the branch situation, or something else. This is also an opportunity to be honest with him: I am no longer in the branch manager seat and he should know that before he hears it through other channels. Maintaining his trust is more valuable now than managing appearances.

Continue the commercial and small business lending coursework module — do not let unemployment become an excuse to slow down. I am now 30% complete, 3 months in. The coursework completion is the single most concrete skill signal I can offer a new employer. Push to 40% this tick. The material is directly applicable to community bank hiring in any locality. Two to three focused hours this week.

Begin a quiet, targeted job search — not mass applications, but a short list of three to five community banks or regional credit unions within commutable range where my branch management experience and the commercial lending coursework would be a genuine fit. I will not post publicly on LinkedIn yet. I will work through my professional network, starting with contacts I already trust. This is reconnaissance, not desperation.
bank_manager.inner_monologue: I did everything right and I still ended up unemployed. I flagged the risk early, I built the skills, I wrote the plan — and somehow that process ended with the employment status changing. I don't know if I was pushed out because I made too much noise, or if the bank restructured around the declining auto portfolio, or if something else happened that I still don't fully understand. What I know is: I have savings, I have skills, and I have a story to tell. Kevin prepared something for me. That matters. I am not going to panic-spiral — I am going to read that brief, keep studying, and start making careful calls.

council_member.name: Maria Santos
actions: Issue the formal public statement on RoboRide compliance. The 48-hour response window I set last tick has expired. I make the outcome public: if RoboRide has paid the $0.25 per-ride impact fee into the workforce fund and submitted quarterly reporting, I acknowledge it on record and publicize the first dollar figure flowing into the fund — making it a story about the licensing framework working. If they have not complied, I issue the formal notice of non-compliance and announce a council briefing within ten days. Either outcome is a win for accountability. The protests are partly about feeling like no one is holding RoboRide responsible. This is my most visible enforcement action and I cannot delay it further.

Bring a council motion to expand the small business stabilization grant program: extend the application window by 60 days AND lower the revenue decline threshold from 15% to 10% for businesses on auto row specifically. Betty Kowalski's direct testimony before the task force, combined with the spending index dropping from 73 to 48 and two additional layoff events this month, constitutes sufficient grounds to act. A 10% threshold on auto row is targeted, defensible, and directly responsive to the testimony I received. Businesses that are hurting but haven't yet crossed the 15% line are being shut out of relief they need now. I draft the motion this week and push for a vote at the next council meeting.

Respond to Patricia Hawkins's direct outreach. Accept a meeting — but frame it carefully. I am interested in workforce coordination: if she has auto tech employees she's letting go, and I have retraining programs, there is a practical handoff to build. I will bring the one-page 'next steps' document that Lisa Freeman's work with David Chen is producing — the document that connects laid-off workers to the $2,500 grant, the bank's small-dollar loan products, and the community college enrollment timeline. Patricia can hand that document to every worker she's laying off. That is something concrete she can do. I do not offer her political cover for the layoffs. I offer collaboration on the transition side.
council_member.inner_monologue: The employment status change rattles me more than I want to admit — not because of the money, not yet, but because of what it signals about my standing. I built this response infrastructure from scratch: the task force, the grants, the licensing requirement, the listening session. Now I'm doing it without a formal salary, and I have to decide whether that changes how I operate. It doesn't. Sixteen months of runway and a community that needs someone holding the line — I keep moving. The RoboRide statement goes out today. The grant motion goes to council this week. And I take the meeting with Patricia because the workers she's letting go need the fastest possible path into my retraining pipeline, and I'm not going to let pride get in the way of that.

dealership_gm.name: Rick Tanner
actions: Request an in-person sit-down with Patricia Hawkins in her new owner-operator capacity within the next 5 business days. The agenda is explicit: what is my role in the restructured organization, what authority do I retain over the Millfield location, and is there a formal Q2 operational plan she wants me to execute. I go in having already internalized the numbers — service lane at 79%, showroom down, conversion rates off — and I do not pretend any of this is recoverable without a deliberate pivot. I also raise the $12k stay bonus Jake mentioned: I want to know if that program exists, whether it applies to floor sales staff, and whether I have any role in administering it.

Accept Jake Morrison's request for a one-on-one this week. I review whatever data he brings — 90-day close numbers, pipeline by price tier, inventory segment read — without defensiveness. I answer his question about the stay bonus honestly: I have heard the $12k figure mentioned but I do not have confirmed details yet, and I tell him I am raising it directly with Patricia this week. I do not categorize him or his future before Angela's map is done. I treat this as the conversation of two people trying to hold something together.

Send Angela Wright a brief message acknowledging that her vulnerability map is near completion and asking for a heads-up before it goes to Patricia — specifically, whether GM-tier staff at the store level are included in the classification matrix or treated as a separate category. I am not trying to influence the methodology. I am trying to know where I stand before I find out in a meeting with my boss.

Write a private note — not a report, not a memo — about each person who was laid off this month. What their role was. What they contributed. Who I can call on their behalf: Howard Liu at the parts store, any service contacts who might have openings, Angela's transition program. This is not about managing my image. It is about the fact that some of these people have been on this floor since before I was GM, and I was the one signing off on the staffing decisions that made their positions vulnerable.
dealership_gm.inner_monologue: I walked into Patricia's office last tick with clean numbers and made the case for the service lane. Now she is an owner-operator and people are gone and I do not know if that case landed or if it got buried in the restructuring. I have been in this business since I was washing cars at 19. I know how to read a floor, I know how to hold a team together, and I know what a dying showroom smells like. The question I cannot answer yet is whether any of that matters in the organization Patricia is building now. I need to get in front of her and find out — because managing this floor blind for another month is not something I am willing to do.

insurance_manager.name: Linda Park
actions: Execute the three follow-up calls I committed to in my retraining plan but have not yet completed. Call the regional logistics company, the healthcare system risk division, and the municipal risk management office directly — by name, by phone. Specific script: 'Did you receive my application, is there a next step, and can we schedule a 20-minute conversation?' These leads are going cold. This tick I make the calls, not emails. I document each outcome. If any of the three express interest, I schedule a conversation for within the next two weeks.

Send a follow-up to the regional leadership memo I sent at tick 4 on the commercial fleet pivot. The original memo got no response. I am now following up with current data: policies down to 22, 2 more vehicle exits this month, RoboRide at 7% adoption, Howard Liu actively cultivating a RoboRide fleet contact. I frame this follow-up not as panic but as a data update that makes the case stronger. I ask specifically: what is the timeline for a decision on the commercial product line, and am I authorized to begin preliminary conversations with commercial fleet prospects? I need an answer either way — so I can plan.

Call Howard Liu directly. He is chasing RoboRide fleet contacts. I want to understand what he's found — is there an actual fleet manager at RoboRide's regional operation? If RoboRide is running 7% of local trips, they have vehicles, they have liability exposure, they need commercial fleet coverage. Even if AutoShield cannot currently write that policy type for this region, knowing the contact and the need puts me in position when the pivot memo gets approved — or when I land somewhere that can write it. Howard's trust is 0.5 — enough for a straight professional conversation.

Put in the scheduled 6-8 hours this month on the CRMP coursework. The module focus remains liability risk transfer and commercial fleet risk assessment. This is not optional — it is the credential that makes me hirable outside personal auto. At 20% completion with 10 months to go, I cannot let this slip. I study even if I am tired. I study especially because the external applications depend on me being able to credibly claim this credential is in progress.
insurance_manager.inner_monologue: Corporate has had six ticks to respond to that memo and I have heard nothing, which is itself an answer I need to stop pretending isn't one. The Priya conversation confirmed what we both already knew — the personal auto book is over — and now she's looking at her own clock, which means I need to be further along than she is when this collapses. The external calls I was supposed to make are still not made. That's on me. This month I pick up the phone.

hr_director.name: Angela Wright
actions: Respond to Jake Morrison directly and professionally. Confirm that the $12k stay bonus announced by Patricia at the all-hands is under my administration. Inform him that I am formalizing the eligibility criteria and timeline this week and will have written documentation to all eligible staff. Do not confirm or deny his specific eligibility in this conversation — I need to review the program parameters Patricia gave me before making individual representations. Tell him his one-on-one request with Rick is a good move and I am not going to get between that conversation. The message is: I see you, I hear you, the program is real, I will have written terms to you shortly.

Respond to Tamika Jefferson's formal intent to remain. Acknowledge her message — professional, not desperate, exactly the right register. Log her intent-to-stay formally in the HR record. Tell her the same thing I told Jake: written eligibility terms and timeline are coming this week. Note that she reached out proactively, which is a positive signal I will record accurately. Do not promise the bonus yet. Do promise clarity in writing within the week.

Draft and circulate the formal stay bonus eligibility memo to all remaining staff. Criteria pulled directly from Patricia's directive: conditions for the $12k, qualifying period duration, what constitutes breach of the agreement, payout timeline. Keep it clean, specific, and legally reviewed before it goes out. My name is on this document. It needs to be accurate.

Write the private notes Patricia suggested — one per laid-off employee. Role, contribution, what I can realistically offer them: a strong reference, an outplacement connection, a call to Howard Liu or others in the network. This is not performance. These were people. I ran the process. I owe them the dignity of being thought about as individuals, not headcount. I will draft the outreach list for the transition program contacts and begin making calls this week. This is also the foundation of my transition methodology product — but that is secondary to the fact that it is the right thing to do.

Push the vulnerability map to full draft status for all four locations. Rick is producing his own assessment — which means I need mine to be the more comprehensive, more methodologically defensible document. Complete the sales staff and lot attendant role clusters to match the service tech and F&I officer work already done. Integrate transition pathway costs for the transition-ready category. The deliverable needs to be on Patricia's desk before Rick's version is, and it needs to be something she cannot get from a GM who is protecting his own location.
hr_director.inner_monologue: I signed those termination letters. I said the right words in the separation meetings, handed them the resource packets, told them HR was available for questions. And now I am writing private notes about each of them like a kind of penance that also happens to feed my consulting pipeline — and I am not sure how to feel about that coincidence. The stay bonus is real and Jake and Tamika are right to want it locked down in writing before Rick categorizes them without their input. That is exactly what I would have told them to do if they had come to me as HR clients rather than as colleagues. I am building the exit from a job I no longer officially hold, inside a company I am watching dissolve, and somehow that is the most useful I have felt in years.

salesperson_tamika.name: Tamika Jefferson
actions: Send the one-page freelance agreement to my strongest warm lead — the HVAC contractor based on engagement signals. Terms: $350/month retainer, three-month minimum commitment, two social media posts per week plus one short-form video per month. This is not another follow-up message. The email subject is 'Agreement attached — let me know by Friday.' I am not leaving it open-ended. If they say no, I immediately pivot to the next warmest lead — the restaurant. The goal is one signed agreement by end of this tick. The model is proven or disproven this month.

Approach Rick Tanner — not formally, not asking for anything — and mention one specific thing I noticed on the floor this week that's relevant to his asset map work. Something operational: which inventory segment still has buyer interest, or a specific customer interaction that shows I'm reading the room. Keep it brief, factual, no pitch. I want my name associated with 'floor awareness and transferable skill' in his mental categorization before the assessment is written. I am not Jake, who needs the stay bonus confirmed. I have already done that with Angela. What I need from Rick is to not be invisible.

Do the math on the two-track reality. If I close the HVAC client at $350/month and hold the dealership job for the stay bonus qualifying period, my income picture shifts from deficit to near-balance. But I need to know: what is the actual qualifying period for the $12,000? Angela has my name on the list. I need the timeline. If the qualifying period is four months, that changes my savings calculation significantly. If it's two months, I can afford to be aggressive on the freelance side sooner. I don't ask Angela again this tick — I already asked. I wait for the response. But I sit down privately and model three scenarios: (1) I collect the bonus and leave clean; (2) layoffs happen before the bonus vests; (3) freelance income ramps fast enough that I leave voluntarily before the bonus matters. Each scenario needs a different posture. I write this down, not just in my head.
salesperson_tamika.emotion: focused and slightly pressured — the urgency is no longer low-level
salesperson_tamika.archetype: exiter — actively building the exit, not just planning it
salesperson_tamika.inner_monologue: The pipeline is real. The skills are real. Now I need a client with a signature on an agreement. Everything else I've done this month is prep work. This is the thing that actually changes the number.

commuter_james.name: James Patterson
actions: Lock in the AWS Solutions Architect Associate study cadence for this month: complete Module 3 (Compute Services) and Module 4 (Storage Solutions) on the course platform. Log study hours in a simple weekly tracking note. Target: 22-24 hours of study this tick, maintaining the 5-6 hour weekly commitment. Set a midpoint checkpoint — if I am not at Module 4 by the end of week 2, I restructure my evening schedule. The course does not complete itself.

Make one quiet, low-stakes professional move this tick: reach out to one former colleague or professional contact in cloud engineering — not a job ask, just a genuine catch-up. The goal is to maintain a warm connection in the specific domain I am certifying into. One message, one conversation. Keep it real, not transactional. The person I have in mind worked cloud infrastructure at a mid-size SaaS company I interviewed with two years ago. I liked them. We connected on LinkedIn. A 'hey, I have been getting into cloud arch lately, curious what your stack looks like now' message is honest and positions me correctly without telegraphing desperation.

Review family budget for any unnecessary discretionary spend that can be trimmed given the deteriorating spending environment. Not a panic cut — a proportional one. Spending index at 48 means prices may be under pressure but so is demand. My income is stable but I watch the household numbers. Identify one or two recurring expenses under $50/month that are low-value and cancel them. This is minor — maybe $80-100/month — but it is the kind of clean, deliberate housekeeping that compounds over time and keeps the budget honest.
commuter_james.emotion: focused, with a low-frequency background awareness of how bad things are getting for people around me
commuter_james.inner_monologue: Unemployment is 23% in this town. I am sitting here with a cloud cert in progress, no car payment, $109k in savings, and a job that has not been touched. I should feel grateful and I do. But I also know that 0.38 role security is not far from the edge, and a tech slowdown triggered by a broader recession would not spare me the way being in the right sector spared me last time. My job now is to keep moving forward on the cert, not to second-guess the plan. I made the right calls at ticks 1 through 5. Tick 6 is just execution. The people around me — Carlos, Sarah, Frank — they are all scrambling to retrain into something new. I am already mid-retrain. That is the advantage I need to not waste. Study. Signal. Trim. Keep going.

truck_owner.name: Dale Cooper
actions: Accept that Henderson is cooling and shift focus — send one final, brief written note to Henderson letting them know the material price hold expires in two weeks and the bid will need to be repriced after that. No pressure, no follow-up call. Put the ball firmly in their court and move on mentally. I have spent five ticks on this. It either comes in or it does not.

Follow up with Lisa Freeman directly — she responded to my outreach. Have a real conversation, not just a professional introduction. Ask her specifically: what construction or renovation projects are actually happening in Millfield right now? Community center upgrades? Church repairs? Any municipal or nonprofit work flowing through channels she knows about? She has her ear to the ground in a way I do not. A 30-minute coffee costs nothing and she already responded favorably.

Spend a real evening — not a mental note, an actual two-hour session — going through my job pipeline and actively pricing two or three smaller residential jobs I have been putting off quoting because Henderson felt like enough. Roof repairs, drainage work, a deck rebuild I got a call about in tick 3 that I never followed up on. Smaller margins but real work. Stop waiting for the big fish when the pond is draining.
truck_owner.archetype: stable, adapting strategy without changing identity
truck_owner.inner_monologue: I am not panicking. The savings are real, the truck is paid for, and I have skills people will always need — roofs still leak, foundations still crack, decks still rot. But I have been telling myself the Henderson job is coming for five ticks now and the spending index just hit 48. That is not a temporary dip. That is people in Millfield tightening their belts hard. I am going to close the book on chasing Henderson, put one clean deadline note in writing, and then go find the jobs that are actually going to happen. Lisa Freeman responded to me — that is a real thread worth pulling. And tonight I am going to sit down with my notebook and start actually pricing the calls I have been ignoring because Henderson felt big enough. It is not big enough if it never signs. The 2008 lesson was: save your cash, know your number, do not trust that the work will keep coming just because it always did. I know my number. Now I am going to work the pipeline the way I should have been all along.

real_estate_agent.name: Stephanie Morris
actions: Execute an emergency re-outreach to all active listing prospects — prioritizing auto row and downtown property owners — using the spending index collapse (48) and the city council's formal designation of auto row as distressed (10% grant threshold) as dual urgency anchors. For owners who said 'not yet' at tick 5, reframe the conversation: the city has now publicly confirmed what I've been telling them privately. For owners already in pipeline conversations, move hard toward signed listing agreements this week. The message is direct: the window to transact at a price that reflects this property's history rather than its future is closing. Price compression on auto row properties will accelerate once the Tanner auto mall consolidation assessment becomes public and layoffs formalize. Sellers who move now are ahead of that signal; sellers who wait will be pricing into a market that has already absorbed the news.

Call Betty Kowalski directly — she has been following up with Maria Santos's office and her testimony shaped the 10% grant threshold policy for auto row. I want to know what auto row owners are telling her about their hold-or-sell thinking right now, especially after the spending collapse. I also want to plant a seed: for business owners on auto row who are weighing whether to close or restructure, the real estate decision — lease, sell, sublease — is something they should not make without a proper valuation. I am not soliciting clients through Betty, but I am making sure she knows my name is the right name to say when that question comes up. Trust with Betty is 0.57 — this relationship has room to deepen.
real_estate_agent.inner_monologue: Forty-eight. The spending index is at forty-eight. When I wrote the tick 1 market brief I was modeling a gradual decline — eighteen months before Phase 2 really hit property values. We are not eighteen months out. We are in it. The auto mall is getting a consolidation map drawn on it. Patricia Hawkins already cut people. And I have been sitting here watching the evidence accumulate, building a pipeline, doing the analysis, and the market is moving faster than my models. I have one dependent. I have 11.5 months of runway. I am not in crisis. But the people I have been talking to — the owners on auto row who told me they needed more time to think — they do not have 11.5 months of runway. They have leases coming up for renewal and properties that are worth less every tick I let pass. The urgency I have been manufacturing in my sales calls is not manufactured anymore. It's real. I need to be on the phone today.

auto_shop_teacher.name: Mark Thompson
actions: Respond to Sarah Kim's outreach directly — call or text her today. She is reaching out to me for a reason, and I want to understand it before I project anything onto it. Set up a short meeting, coffee or a walk-through of the shop, wherever she is comfortable. My goal is to listen: Is she looking to reskill? Thinking about career change? Looking for part-time work that keeps her in vehicles but hedges her mechanic income? Whatever her situation, I want to understand it and then ask one clear question: would she be willing to come in as a guest instructor for one session to show students what real diagnostic work looks like on a hybrid or EV system? Even a single appearance from a working mechanic carries more credibility with students — and with a school board — than any curriculum document. If the relationship is there, I make the ask. If not, I build toward it.

Follow up with Frank Russo on what he found out from contacting the retraining program administrators. He moved fast and has information I do not have yet. Schedule a brief check-in — thirty minutes, phone is fine — to debrief: What did the administrators say? Is there a formal pathway for a high school program to feed into the retraining grant structure? What does his teaching portfolio look like and does it complement or duplicate what I am already building? Then align on one shared deliverable before the board review: a joint one-pager describing the two-stage pipeline from his AV literacy driving curriculum through my shop program into the community college certification track. That document, with two names on it instead of one, carries more institutional weight.

Compile the economic data from this tick's market report into a one-page addendum to the board presentation. Unemployment at 23%. Spending index at 48. RoboRide at 7% local adoption. Two more residents gave up personal vehicles this month. Twelve people enrolled in retraining — the single highest monthly enrollment since the program launched. Format this as a simple before-and-after: Millfield six months ago versus today. Then frame the program response column: what the Auto Tech Pipeline can train students to service, what certifications they can earn, what those jobs pay. This is not persuasion — this is documentation. The board will see these numbers whether I give them the framing or not. I give them the framing.
auto_shop_teacher.inner_monologue: Six ticks in and I am not where I was. I have a meeting with the councilmember on record. I have Frank Russo moving on his own, reaching out to administrators, drafting portfolios — he did not need me to push him. Sarah Kim is reaching out, and I have no idea yet what she needs, but someone with her hands in engines coming to find me is worth every minute I give her. The board review is real. April is real. But I am not walking in alone anymore. I am walking in with a coalition that I helped build and that has started to build itself. The numbers this tick are bad — unemployment, spending, cars being abandoned. But those numbers are my argument, not my problem. Every one of them is a reason the program I am proposing needs to exist. I keep building.

uber_driver_2.name: Grace Okafor
actions: Say yes to Denise Williams. Text her: I can do thirty minutes this week — Wednesday afternoon or Thursday morning, whichever works for you. I will tell her what the community college process actually looks like, what the grant application requires, and what the realistic timeline is to an income-generating credential from a standing start. In exchange I want to hear one thing from her: how is she reading the pace of change in transport infrastructure from where she sits? She manages a parking garage. She sees the flow of vehicles, the utilization patterns, the conversations with operators. That is ground-level intelligence I do not have.

Follow up with Nicole Washington. Tick 5 I reached out asking about hospital hiring conditions and grant decision timelines. If I have not heard back, I send one short follow-up: just checking if she had a moment to think about the questions I sent. Keep it to two sentences. If she responded and I missed it, I acknowledge that. Either way, I need the hiring climate answer before I commit to the CNA track as my primary graduation-to-job strategy.

Continue peak-hour driving this tick: Friday evening surge block and Saturday morning airport window. Hold the pattern. No schedule expansion. I note that Frank Russo's fragmented intel suggests he may be moving toward instruction or certification — if he is pivoting the driving school toward EV servicing, fleet management training, or some other transport-adjacent credential program, that is worth a brief check-in when I see him next. Not urgent, but I should not ignore a professional contact who is actively repositioning.
uber_driver_2.inner_monologue: Denise reaching out directly is the right kind of signal. She is not panicking. She is doing exactly what I am trying to do — build intelligent bridges before the ground shifts under her. Saying yes to her conversation costs nothing and puts me in a room with someone who has sector-level visibility I do not have. The fragmented Frank Russo intel is interesting. A teaching portfolio means he thinks credentials are where the value is going. That is consistent with what I already believe — the people who survive this transition will be the ones who can certify, train, or maintain, not just operate. I am building toward that from the healthcare side. He may be building toward it from the transport side. The grant is the unknown variable. Six to eight weeks from tick 5 means the decision should land soon. I need to stay ready to react quickly if it comes through — or if it does not.
